newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX Hub natgas ends up, then gains more on AGAs.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX Hub natgas ends up, then gains more on AGAs.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natgas futures, helped by firmer physical prices, ended higher Wednesday in a fairly active session, then moved up more after an unexpectedly-bullish weekly inventory report, sources said.

August climbed 3.1 cents to close at $2.148 per million British thermal units, then climbed to $2.168 on ACCESS shortly after the AGA data. September settled two cents higher at $2.093. Most others ended steady to up two cents.
"People were expecting a low (AGA) number but it's an unusually low number and it's definitely bullish," said one Midwest trader.
AGA said Wednesday that U.S. gas stocks rose last week by 58 bcf, well below average estimates in the 75-80 bcf range. Overall stocks are now 183 bcf, or 11 percent, above year-ago levels.

Eastern inventories increased by 48 bcf last week and were still 56 bcf, or six percent, over last year. Consuming region west storage, which gained 10 bcf last week, continued to lag 1996 levels by about six percent. Stocks in the producing region were unchanged for the week and still 41 percent above year-ago.
But despite bullish AGA data, few expected prices to rally much from here, particularly with stocks in good shape and little extreme weather forecast for the balance of the month.

Chart traders agreed August was stuck in a range, with support still at $2.07 and then at the $2.051 low from July 8. Major trendline resistance this week remained in the low-$2.20s, with further selling likely at the $2.29 and $2.36 prominent highs. Most said it would take an August close above the trendline to turn sentiment decidedly bullish.
In the cash Wednesday, Gulf Coast prices firmed three cents to the mid-to-high teens. Midcon pipes were four cents higher at about $2.10. New York city gate gas was up slightly at about $2.40.
The NYMEX Henry Hub 12-month strip gained 1.8 cents to $2.201. NYMEX said 47,141 contracts traded, up slightly from Tuesday's revised tally of 45,913.

On the KCBT, August finished up 2.9 cents at $2.065, while deferreds ended one cent higher. The East/West spread widened by 0.2 cent to 8.3 cents (NYMEX premium). KCBT said 492 lots traded, up sharply from Tuesday's total of 185.
